adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy goroutines derive their ctx from the request ctx (also L110, L135, L163), which net/http/apiserver cancels once the handler returns, so legacy SQL writes race a canceled ctx and routinely fail with "context canceled" instead of using context.WithoutCancel.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection the legacy operation is moved into a `go func()` that does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` using the same `ctx` passed into the request handler. Because the goroutine runs after the method returns, it can inherit cancellation from the parent ctx; `WithTimeoutCause` does not detach from parent cancellation. This makes the async legacy writes prone to immediate `context canceled` failures, defeating the intended background write behavior. The diff shows this pattern in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Legacy write errors in every goroutine (L56, L113, L140, L166) are discarded without any log line, so a legacy store that fails on every write leaves only an unlabeled boolean metric and no diagnosable trace.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes were changed to fire-and-forget goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). Inside those goroutines the returned legacy errors are only fed into recordLegacyDuration/recordStorageDuration and are otherwise ignored (no log.Error / no propagation). E.g. Create: `_, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...)` then `d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)`; Delete: `_, _, err := d.Legacy.Delete(...)` then `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)`; Update similarly. This is a concrete observability/diagnosability regression, but since mode3 explicitly returns the unified-store result and treats legacy as best-effort, it’s not strictly a functional correctness defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — DeleteCollection records the legacy result via recordStorageDuration, so legacy delete-collection failures are counted as unified-storage metrics and the legacy error dashboard stays green.

adjudication.rationale:
In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the async legacy call incorrectly reports its duration/error via `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`:
```go
_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)
d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
```
This misattributes legacy failures and timings to unified-storage metrics, matching the finding that legacy delete-collection failures won’t show up in legacy metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Unified-storage Create failure is recorded as a legacy error (recordLegacyDuration) and never as a storage error (same bug in Update at L129), inflating legacy error rates and hiding storage failures.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create() measures `startStorage := time.Now()` before calling `d.Storage.Create(...)`, but on storage error it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of recording a storage failure (and never calls `recordStorageDuration` on that error path). The same pattern exists in Update(): after `startStorage := time.Now()` and a failed `d.Storage.Update(...)`, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` rather than a storage-duration/error metric. This will misattribute unified-store failures to legacy metrics and hide storage error rates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Delete success records the storage metric with the object name as the kind label, mislabeling the series and creating unbounded label cardinality (one Prometheus series per object name).

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy Update receives the raw objInfo instead of wrapping the unified result (the removed updateWrapper), so PATCH/apply is recomputed against legacy's own possibly divergent state and admission runs again, leaving stores with different content/resourceVersion.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Update the previous implementation computed the updated object once and used an updateWrapper so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update would operate on the same unified result. This diff removes that logic and now calls `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` and later (async) `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` with the original `objInfo` (no wrapper, no reuse of the unified-store result). For UpdatedObjectInfo implementations that derive the new object from the current stored object (e.g., patch/apply-style updates), this can cause the legacy write to recompute against legacy’s own state and produce different content/resourceVersion than unified storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Independent unordered goroutines per request mean a create followed quickly by delete (or two updates) for the same object can run out of order in legacy, resurrecting deleted objects or leaving stale data with no reconciliation.

adjudication.rationale: In mode3 the diff changes legacy writes/deletes/updates to run asynchronously in independent goroutines (Create: `go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, Delete: `go func(){ d.Legacy.Delete(...) }()`, Update: `go func(){ d.Legacy.Update(...) }()`). There is no per-object ordering, serialization, or reconciliation shown. That means two requests on the same object (e.g., Create then quickly Delete, or two Updates) can race so the legacy operations execute out of order relative to each other, potentially leaving legacy with stale/resurrected state even though unified storage is correct. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff (previously legacy calls were synchronous).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134 — Update issued while the async legacy Create is still pending fails with NotFound in legacy (forceAllowCreate=false), silently and permanently losing the update in legacy.

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3, Create writes to Storage synchronously but performs Legacy.Create asynchronously in a goroutine (with a 10s timeout) and does not block before returning (dualwriter_mode3.go Create: `created, err := d.Storage.Create...` then `go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`). Update likewise writes to Storage synchronously and performs Legacy.Update asynchronously, ignoring any returned error except for metrics (no log/propagation/retry) (Update: `res, async, err := d.Storage.Update...` then `go func(){ _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(...) }()`). This makes it possible for a client to Create (returns before legacy write finishes) and then immediately Update with `forceAllowCreate=false`; the Legacy.Update may run before Legacy.Create completes and can fail with NotFound, and that failure is effectively dropped, permanently losing the update in legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:112 — Legacy Delete reuses the client's DeleteOptions preconditions (UID/resourceVersion from unified storage), which may not match legacy, so legacy deletes get rejected and only a metric notices.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, the legacy delete is invoked asynchronously and reuses the same *metav1.DeleteOptions passed to the unified store delete: `d.Legacy.Delete(ctx, name, deleteValidation, options)` inside the goroutine. The diff also removes the prior explicit error handling/logging for legacy delete failures (previously non-NotFound errors were logged), so a legacy rejection (e.g., due to preconditions in DeleteOptions not matching legacy state) would now be effectively silent except for `recordLegacyDuration(...)`. However, the diff alone does not prove that unified and legacy preconditions will actually differ in practice, so it’s a concrete risk/edge-case concern rather than a definitively verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — The goroutine keeps using the caller's obj/options pointers after Create returns while the unified store and the response path may still reference or mutate them, which is a data race under -race and can send legacy a mutated object.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, after the unified-store Create completes, a goroutine is launched that calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ..., options) using the same runtime.Object and *metav1.CreateOptions values captured from the caller. Since Create returns immediately after starting the goroutine, the caller (or other code) may legally reuse/mutate those objects/options after return, which can race with the goroutine under -race and can cause the legacy write to observe mutated state. The diff shows no deep-copy of obj/options before the async call, so the finding is grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Each write spawns an unbounded fire-and-forget goroutine that can live up to 10s, so a slow or hung legacy DB under load piles up goroutines and DB connections with no backpressure or concurrency limit.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now launch a `go func()` to perform the legacy write/delete asynchronously (e.g., Create: `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(...10s...); _, err := d.Legacy.Create(...)}()`), and the handler returns immediately. There is no concurrency limiting, queueing, or backpressure, so under sustained load a slow legacy backend can cause an unbounded number of goroutines to accumulate for up to ~10s each, potentially increasing resource usage (goroutines, in-flight legacy calls/DB connections). This is a concrete scalability/operational concern introduced by the diff, not a directly provable functional correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:53 — Legacy and storage mocks share one mock.Mock and tests never wait for or assert the async legacy call, so the tests pass whether legacy writes happen, fail, or hit the wrong store.

adjudication.rationale: In the new mode3 tests, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `*mock.Mock` (`m := &mock.Mock{}`), and expectations are set on method names like `Create`, `Update`, etc. Because both storages invoke the same mock with identical method names and many args are `mock.Anything`, a call intended for Storage can satisfy the Legacy expectation (and vice versa). Additionally, mode3 production code now performs legacy writes in goroutines (`go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/... }()` etc.), but the tests neither wait for these goroutines nor call `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, so they can pass even if the async legacy call never happens, fails, or is matched by the wrong store call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:522 — The new Mode3 integration runs check the legacy /api/playlists endpoint, which is served through the k8s dual writer (reading unified) when kubernetesPlaylists is on, so they cannot detect missing or failed legacy SQL writes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds new Mode3 integration subtests in `pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go` (configuring `DualWriterDesiredModes` and feature toggles) but does not show what endpoints `doPlaylistTests` exercises (e.g., `/api/playlists`) or how reads/writes are routed when `FlagKubernetesPlaylists` is enabled. Since the alleged inability to detect missing legacy SQL writes depends on behavior not present in the shown diff, the finding is not verifiable from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts d.Log rather than the enriched log into ctx, so downstream logs lose the name/kind/method context.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Create records a unified-storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, so it shows up as a legacy failure in metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create(), when d.Storage.Create(...) returns an error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) even though the failed operation was the unified storage call. This would misattribute a storage-side failure as a legacy failure in metrics; it should record storage duration (e.g., recordStorageDuration) on that path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Update records a unified-storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the error path after `d.Storage.Update(...)` logs "unable to update in storage" but then calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. Since the failure occurred in unified storage, this should be `recordStorageDuration(...)` (and it also passes `startStorage`, reinforcing it’s the storage timing). This misattributes metrics and is verifiable directly from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — The async legacy DeleteCollection records its result with recordStorageDuration, so legacy timings and errors are counted as unified-storage metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine ends with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`, even though it is measuring the legacy store call (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`). This will attribute legacy latency/error to storage/unified-store metrics, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — The async legacy goroutines (here and at lines 110, 135, 163) derive their ctx from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the handler returns, so legacy writes can be cancelled before they finish and the 10s timeout gives no protection.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3 methods (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection), the legacy write is done in a goroutine with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` where `ctx` is the request-scoped context passed into the handler. Because the derived timeout context is a child of the request context, it will be canceled as soon as the request context is canceled (commonly when the handler returns), potentially aborting the async legacy write immediately and making the 10s timeout ineffective. This can cause the intended background legacy write to not complete (data divergence).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Delete success passes `name` as the kind label to recordStorageDuration instead of options.Kind, giving the wrong label and unbounded label cardinality.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:100 — Delete dropped the old NotFound handling, so an object that exists only in legacy now returns early and is never deleted from legacy, leaving orphans.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, the previous implementation special-cased `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` from `d.Storage.Delete(...)` and still proceeded to call `d.Legacy.Delete(...)`. The new code returns early on *any* storage error (`if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`) and only triggers the legacy delete goroutine on success. Therefore, if the object is missing in Storage (NotFound) but present in Legacy, legacy deletion will never run, leaving legacy orphans—exactly as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Removing updateWrapper means legacy now re-runs objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own old object instead of receiving the object unified storage persisted, so the two stores can diverge or fail on resourceVersion preconditions.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() previously computed the updated object once (against Storage’s current object), then used updateWrapper to force both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update to apply the exact same already-updated object (and for Legacy, it even wrapped the final object returned from Storage: `updated: obj`). The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` without any wrapper (and without passing Storage’s persisted object). Given the Kubernetes `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` contract, this means Legacy will likely call `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, oldLegacyObj)` and can produce a different result than Storage (or fail due to different resourceVersion/preconditions), causing divergence between stores. This behavior change is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:134 — Legacy writes run in unordered fire-and-forget goroutines, so a quick create->update->delete sequence can reach legacy out of order (e.g. an update before its create), leaving legacy inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy mutations are now executed asynchronously in independent goroutines (e.g., Create: `go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, Update: `go func(){ d.Legacy.Update(...) }()`, Delete: `go func(){ d.Legacy.Delete(...) }()`). There is no per-object ordering/serialization, so a caller doing create→update→delete quickly can have the legacy goroutines scheduled/executed out of order (e.g., legacy Update/Delete runs before legacy Create completes), leaving the legacy store inconsistent with the unified store. This behavior is introduced by the diff (previously legacy calls were synchronous).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — The async Legacy.Create shares `obj` with the in-flight request (Storage.Create may return or mutate the same object while the response is serialized), which risks a data race.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the function calls `d.Storage.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` and then returns `created` while also launching a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` using the same `obj` reference. Since the legacy write runs concurrently with the caller’s subsequent processing/serialization of the returned object (and storage/legacy Create implementations commonly mutate the passed-in object’s metadata), this introduces a concrete risk of concurrent access to the same underlying object without synchronization or deep-copying.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:38 — The metric and log "kind" label uses options.Kind, which is the TypeMeta of the Create/Get/Delete options object (usually empty), not the resource kind, so per-kind metrics are meaningless.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the new logging/metrics labels for "kind" are sourced from options.Kind (e.g., Create/Get/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection use options.Kind; List uses options.Kind from ListOptions). The diff shows call sites/tests frequently pass &metav1.CreateOptions{} / &metav1.GetOptions{} / &metav1.DeleteOptions{} / &metav1.UpdateOptions{} without setting TypeMeta.Kind, meaning the "kind" label will often be empty and thus not useful for per-kind metrics/logging. This affects observability rather than core correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete puts d.Log into the context instead of the enriched `log`, so downstream logs lose the name, kind and method values.
matched_golden_ids: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same problem: the context is populated with d.Log instead of the enriched `log` that includes name/kind/method fields, causing downstream logs to miss those values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:56 — Legacy write failures in the async goroutines are no longer logged (only a metric bool is recorded), so divergence errors are silently swallowed.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes were changed from synchronous calls that logged errors (e.g., prior Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection used log.Error/WithValues(...).Error on legacy failures) to async goroutines that ignore the returned error except for recording a success/fail boolean via recordLegacyDuration. For example, Create now runs d.Legacy.Create(...) in a goroutine and does not log errObjectSt; Delete and Update similarly omit logging inside the goroutine. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/regression concern (errors can be silently lost), but it doesn’t clearly change the primary API behavior since mode3 already returns the Storage result and treats legacy writes as best-effort.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:40 — The Create storage-failure test only sets up a legacy mock and passes because storage shares the same mock.Mock; no mode3 test waits for or asserts the async legacy calls.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, the “error when creating object in the unified store fails” case only configures `setupLegacyFn` and does not configure any storage `Create` expectation. But both `legacyStoreMock{m, ...}` and `storageMock{m, ...}` are built on the same `*mock.Mock` (`m := &mock.Mock{}`), and the dual-writer calls `Storage.Create` first; that call can satisfy the single `m.On("Create", ...)` expectation and thus simulate a storage failure without ever verifying the intended behavior. Separately, mode3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously via `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection ... }()`, and the tests neither wait for those goroutines nor assert that the legacy calls occurred (no synchronization and no `AssertExpectations`), so the new async legacy side effects aren’t actually tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Storage Create failure is recorded via recordLegacyDuration (copy-paste slip), so storage errors are reported as legacy metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DualWriterMode3.Create() measures `startStorage := time.Now()` and calls `d.Storage.Create(...)`. On error, it logs and then calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, which incorrectly records a *storage* failure as a *legacy* duration/metric (copy-paste mistake). It should record storage duration on the storage call failure (e.g., `recordStorageDuration`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Storage Update failure is recorded via recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, which mislabels the metric.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, after calling `d.Storage.Update(...)`, the error path records the duration using `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. This is a storage operation failure, and it uses the storage start time (`startStorage`), so it should be recorded via `recordStorageDuration`, not `recordLegacyDuration`, otherwise the metric is mislabeled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Async legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded via recordStorageDuration, which mixes legacy timings into storage metrics.
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Delete success metric passes `name` as the kind label where every other call passes options.Kind, causing inconsistent labels and unbounded cardinality.
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the Delete success metric uses `name` as the kind label instead of `options.Kind`, unlike other methods, leading to inconsistent metric labels (and potential high cardinality). This matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — The goroutine + WithTimeoutCause + time.Now + recordLegacyDuration block is copy-pasted across Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection; extract a helper (the metric slips above come from this duplication).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated, near-identical patterns across Mode3 methods: launching a goroutine, wrapping the ctx with `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, errors.New("legacy ... timeout"))`, capturing `time.Now()`, calling the legacy operation, and recording duration (e.g., in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`). This is a concrete maintainability/duplication issue introduced by the change and reasonably suggests extracting a helper. While the finding mentions “metric slips,” the core claim (copy-pasted timeout/metrics goroutine blocks) is directly verifiable from the diff and is not itself a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Magic 10s legacy-write timeout is hard-coded in four places instead of a named constant or config.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy-write goroutines use context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...) with a hard-coded 10s in four methods: Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection. This is verifiable from the diff and is a maintainability/configurability concern rather than a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete stores d.Log in ctx instead of the enriched `log` like the other methods, so downstream logs lose name/kind/method.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the code builds an enriched logger `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then stores the *unenriched* `d.Log` in the context: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`. Other methods in this diff store the enriched `log` in the context (e.g., `Create`, `Get`, `List`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). This is a real behavioral issue: downstream code using `klog.FromContext(ctx)` will lose the added fields (name/kind/method).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Async legacy write errors are only counted in metrics and never logged (earlier code logged them), so legacy divergence cannot be diagnosed.

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes were changed from synchronous calls that logged errors (e.g., previous `log.WithValues(...).Error(err, "unable to create object in legacy storage")`) to goroutines for `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection` that only call `recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)` and do not log `err` anywhere inside the goroutine. This makes legacy-write failures largely invisible except via metrics, reducing diagnosability, but it does not by itself prove a functional correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Legacy Update gets the raw objInfo rather than an updateWrapper holding the storage result (the pattern the old code used), so legacy recomputes the update separately and can diverge.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, the old Update path computed the updated object once and wrapped objInfo in an updateWrapper so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update used the same computed result. In the new code, Update calls d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...) and then asynchronously calls d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...) with the original objInfo (no wrapper containing the storage result). This means legacy may recompute UpdatedObject independently and can diverge from what was actually persisted in unified storage, defeating dual-write consistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:119 — Comment says Update writes "first to Storage and then to LegacyStorage", but the legacy write is now a fire-and-forget goroutine.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the comment above `Update` says it writes "first to Storage and then to LegacyStorage", implying a synchronous second write. The implementation now performs the legacy write in a fire-and-forget goroutine with a timeout (`go func() { ... d.Legacy.Update(...) }()`), so the function returns before the legacy write completes. This is a doc/behavior mismatch grounded in the diff, but not itself a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:35 — Create/DeleteCollection doc comments (and the constructor comment at line 23) do not mention that the legacy write is asynchronous and best-effort.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the behavior was changed so legacy operations are now executed asynchronously and best-effort (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection start the legacy call in a goroutine with a 10s timeout and do not propagate errors). However, the doc comments still describe these methods (and the mode 3 constructor comment) as simply writing/deleting to both LegacyStorage and Storage without noting the async/best-effort nature. This is a real, diff-grounded documentation mismatch, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:94 — Delete has no doc comment, unlike the other overridden methods.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `func (d *DualWriterMode3) Delete(...)` without a preceding doc comment, while `Create`, `Get`, `List`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` have doc comments. However, this is a documentation/style nit rather than a concrete defect or substantive review issue grounded in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — The unclear name `errObjectSt` (also at line 139) differs from the shadowed `err` used in the Delete/DeleteCollection goroutines.

adjudication.rationale: The cited issue is purely a naming/style nit: `errObjectSt` is just a local variable name used in the legacy Create/Update goroutines, while Delete uses `err`. This does not introduce a correctness defect or broken behavior visible in the diff, and the finding’s focus (“unclear name differs from shadowed err”) is not an important, diff-grounded review concern beyond minor readability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:135 — Goroutine bodies order differently (startLegacy before or after WithTimeoutCause, defer cancel separated by a blank line), which hurts readability across methods.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show inconsistent ordering inside the goroutines (e.g., Create/Update set up WithTimeoutCause then startLegacy; Delete/DeleteCollection record startLegacy before WithTimeoutCause, and the placement of defer cancel varies). However, the finding is purely a readability/style consistency nit and not a verifiable defect or substantial review issue grounded in behavior changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:59 — Returns `err` (always nil at this point) instead of an explicit nil, and the same pattern repeats at lines 116, 143, and 169.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the methods (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) return `..., err` where `err` is the error value from the immediately preceding Storage call. On the success path `err` will indeed be `nil`, but returning the variable (instead of an explicit `nil`) is not a behavioral defect; it’s at most a style nit. The diff does not show any incorrect `err` value being returned due to this pattern at the cited spots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:37 — var method = "..."` is used for fixed strings where a const or `:=` would be idiomatic, and mode3Str is declared mid-file between methods.

adjudication.rationale: The cited issues are purely idiomatic/style nits: the diff does show repeated `var method = "..."` assignments for fixed strings and `const mode3Str = "3"` placed after `Mode()`, but neither affects correctness or behavior, nor is it a specific non-bug architectural risk grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: go.work.sum:408 — Unrelated go.work.sum churn in a dual-writer change, including a duplicate of the apimachinery go.mod line already at line 404.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows go.work.sum changes that appear unrelated to the dual-writer logic changes, and it does introduce a duplicate line: `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod ...` exists before the added block and is added again within the new lines. This is real, diff-grounded go.work.sum churn/duplication, but it’s not clearly a functional defect in the PR’s runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:41 — The "unified store fails" Create case only sets up a Legacy expectation and passes because ls and us share one mock.Mock, so the storage/legacy setup split is misleading.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `*mock.Mock` (`m := &mock.Mock{}` then `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `us := storageMock{m, s}`). In the "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case, only `setupLegacyFn` is provided and it sets `m.On("Create", ..., failingObj, ...).Return(nil, error)`, while `setupStorageFn` is nil. Since Mode3 `Create` calls `d.Storage.Create(...)` first, that storage call will match the shared mock's `Create` expectation, so the test passes without actually distinguishing legacy vs storage behavior. This is misleading test setup and can mask bugs, but it’s a test-quality issue rather than a runtime defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — Tests never wait for or assert the async legacy calls, so the new goroutine behavior is untested and may race with test teardown.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy operations are now executed asynchronously via `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection ... }()` with a 10s timeout. The new tests in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go set up mock expectations for some legacy calls (e.g., `setupLegacyFn` in Create/Update) but never wait for those goroutines to run and never assert mock expectations (no `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or similar). This leaves the async legacy behavior unverified and can also race, since the same `*mock.Mock` is used by both storage and legacy and may be accessed concurrently by the goroutine and the test thread.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:119 — TestMode3_Get shadows the package-level `p` registry that every other test uses (defined in dualwriter_mode1_test.go).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TestMode3_Get` creating a local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` and passing it to `NewDualWriter`, which would shadow any package-level `p` if one exists. However, the diff does not show a package-level `p` (nor that it is defined in `dualwriter_mode1_test.go`), and the finding doesn’t demonstrate a real defect—using a per-test registry is often intentional to avoid cross-test metric registration conflicts. This is at most a minor consistency/style nit, not a verifiable bug or important issue from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:145 — Stale test-case name "listing ... is not implemented" now that List is implemented.

adjudication.rationale: The cited issue is just a misleading/stale subtest name in `TestMode3_List` (it says "... is not implemented"), while `DualWriterMode3.List` is now implemented in `dualwriter_mode3.go`. This is a minor readability/naming nit and not a verifiable defect or substantive review issue affecting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — Async legacy write ctx derives from the request ctx, which is cancelled once the handler returns, so legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection (lines 51, 110, 135, 163) will often fail immediately; use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) as the parent

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes were changed to run asynchronously in goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). Each goroutine derives its context from the incoming `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` (e.g., Create: `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...); ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }`). If the parent request context is canceled when the handler returns, these async legacy calls will be canceled immediately/early, causing legacy writes to frequently fail or not happen. The diff does not detach the context (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`), so the finding is grounded in the new async behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — Legacy write errors in all four async goroutines (lines 55, 112, 139, 165) are silently dropped with no log, only a metric bool, so legacy/unified divergence is invisible

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are moved into async goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). In each goroutine the returned error is only converted to a boolean for d.recordLegacyDuration(...)/d.recordStorageDuration(...) and is otherwise ignored—there is no log/Error call inside the goroutine, so failures of the legacy side lose the actual error details and aren’t visible in logs (only via a metric flag). This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/reliability concern, but not a strictly verifiable functional correctness defect since the intended behavior appears to be “best-effort legacy writes” in mode 3.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Legacy writes are fire-and-forget with no retry or reconciliation queue, so any transient legacy failure causes permanent divergence while the client is told the write succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes are now executed asynchronously in a goroutine with a 10s timeout and their errors are neither returned to the caller nor retried/reconciled (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection each start `go func() { ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) ... }()` and then return the unified-store result). This makes divergence between Storage and Legacy possible if the legacy operation fails or times out while the client still receives success from the Storage write. The diff itself doesn’t show any retry/reconciliation mechanism being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Goroutines are spawned per request with no bound, tracking, or WaitGroup, so a slow legacy store can pile up to 10s of goroutines per write, and Destroy (line 172) tears down Legacy while writes are still in flight

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now spawn an asynchronous legacy write via `go func() { ... }()` on every successful storage operation, each with a 10s timeout (`context.WithTimeoutCause(..., time.Second*10, ...)`). There is no bounding (worker pool/rate limit), tracking, or synchronization (e.g., WaitGroup) shown in the diff, so under load a slow legacy store can cause many goroutines to accumulate for up to ~10s. However, the specific claim that `Destroy` “tears down Legacy while writes are still in flight” is not directly verifiable from the shown diff because the `Destroy()` implementation is not included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — The legacy Update reuses the raw objInfo instead of wrapping it with the unified-storage result (the updateWrapper was removed), so legacy recomputes the update from its own old object and preconditions/resourceVersion may fail or diverge silently

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, the previous Update implementation explicitly computed the updated object from the unified-store “old” (`old, err := d.Storage.Get(...)` then `updated, err := objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)`) and wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper{updated: updated}` so both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update would apply the exact same updated object. The new code removes this wrapper and passes the raw `objInfo` to the async legacy update (`d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)`) after Storage.Update succeeds. This allows legacy to recompute the update against its own prior state (and potentially different preconditions/resourceVersion), which can diverge from the unified-store result or fail unexpectedly, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:55 — The goroutine hands the same obj pointer to Legacy.Create while the caller may still be serializing or mutating the object returned from Storage.Create, a potential data race

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Create, after Storage.Create returns, a goroutine is launched that calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) using the same `obj` pointer passed into Storage.Create. The diff does not show whether Storage.Create returns/aliases the same object instance (common) or whether callers might mutate/observe it after Create returns, so an actual data race cannot be verified from the diff alone. However, the change clearly introduces asynchronous use of a potentially shared mutable object without copying, which is a concrete, diff-grounded concurrency/ownership concern a reviewer can act on (e.g., deep-copy before launching the goroutine).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — Legacy DeleteCollection outcome is recorded with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, which corrupts both storage and legacy metrics

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection’s async legacy deletion goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` after `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`. This clearly records a legacy operation using the storage-metrics recorder, which will misattribute durations and corrupt both legacy and storage metrics for this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Unified-storage Create failure is recorded as a legacy duration/error (same bug in Update at line 129), so storage failures are misattributed in metrics

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the storage call is timed with `startStorage := time.Now()`, but on unified-store failure it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of recording a storage metric. The same misattribution occurs in `DualWriterMode3.Update`: on `d.Storage.Update` error it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` using `startStorage`. This incorrectly attributes unified-storage failures/durations to legacy metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 — Successful Delete records the object name as the kind metric label, which mislabels the metric and creates unbounded label cardinality

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete(), the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing `name` where other methods consistently pass `options.Kind` as the "kind" label (e.g., Create/Get/List/DeleteCollection all use `options.Kind`). This mislabels the metric and, since `name` varies per object, can create unbounded label cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97 — Delete stores d.Log instead of the enriched log in ctx, so downstream and async legacy logs lose name/kind/method context

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete the code builds an enriched logger `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then sets the context with `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. As a result, `d.Storage.Delete(...)` and the async legacy delete goroutine receive a ctx whose logger lacks the added name/kind/method fields, so any downstream `klog.FromContext(ctx)` logging will miss that context. This is a concrete diff-grounded issue, but it impacts observability/log context rather than correctness of delete behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — Tests use context.Background and never wait for or assert the async legacy calls, so they cannot catch the cancelled-context or dropped-error failure modes

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy operations for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection are now executed asynchronously in `go func()` with a 10s `context.WithTimeoutCause(...)`, and errors are only recorded via metrics (not returned). In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the tests call `dw.Create/Get/List/Delete/DeleteCollection/Update` using `context.Background()` and return immediately after asserting only the unified-store result; they do not block for the legacy goroutine to run nor assert mock expectations (no `AssertExpectations`/sync primitive shown). Therefore these tests cannot detect failure modes specific to the async legacy path (e.g., context timeout/cancellation preventing the legacy call, or legacy errors being dropped/logged).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:53 — Legacy and Storage mocks share one mock.Mock, so expectations are indistinguishable and no test can prove Storage (not Legacy) was written or read.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go the tests instantiate a single `m := &mock.Mock{}` and pass it into both `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}`. Expectations are then set on that shared mock with generic method names like `m.On("Create", ...)`, `m.On("Update", ...)`, etc. Because both mocks expose the same method names, calls from Legacy and Storage are not distinguishable by the mock framework, and broad matchers can let one expectation satisfy the other. This is visible in `TestMode3_Create`: the "unified store fails" case sets only a `Create` expectation in `setupLegacyFn` and none for `setupStorageFn`, yet the Storage.Create call could still match the Legacy `On("Create", ...)` expectation since it’s the same underlying mock. That means the tests cannot reliably prove that reads/writes are happening against Storage vs Legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — Async legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection goroutines are never awaited or asserted (no AssertExpectations/Eventually), so the headline "write to legacy" behavior is untested and the goroutine may run after the test ends.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are performed asynchronously via `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(...) }()`. In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the tests set up mock expectations for legacy calls (e.g., `setupLegacyFn` in `TestMode3_Create` and `TestMode3_Update`) but never wait for the goroutine to run nor assert that it ran (no `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, no eventual/timeout-based assertion). As a result, the intended “also writes to legacy” behavior is not actually verified, and the legacy goroutine can execute after the test case returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — Every test uses context.Background(), so nothing catches that the legacy goroutines derive from the request ctx and get cancelled once the request returns (dualwriter_mode3.go:51,110,135,163).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces async legacy operations in Mode3 (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) that run in goroutines and derive their context from the request `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. In the new tests in `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the calls all use `context.Background()`, so they won’t exercise behavior under a cancellable request context (e.g., cancellation immediately after the primary storage call returns). While it’s a concrete test gap tied to the new async logic, the diff alone doesn’t prove that request contexts will always be cancelled “once the request returns” in the actual call sites, so it’s not strictly verifiable as a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:40 — The "unified store fails" Create case sets up the error via setupLegacyFn and passes only because Storage.Create hits the shared mock's legacy expectation.

adjudication.rationale: In TestMode3_Create, the case named "error when creating object in the unified store fails" only sets an expectation via setupLegacyFn: `m.On("Create", ..., failingObj, ...)`. However, DualWriter mode3 Create calls `d.Storage.Create(...)` first (in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go). Because both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` are backed by the same `*mock.Mock` instance (`m`), the Storage.Create call will match and consume this "legacy" expectation, making the test pass without actually distinguishing which backend failed. This is a real defect in the test: it doesn't verify the intended behavior and can mask regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:129 — Get and List tests do not assert that Legacy is untouched, which drops the 0-legacy-call checks from the old commented-out TestMode3 (and mode1 uses AssertNotCalled).

adjudication.rationale: In the new Mode3 tests, `TestMode3_Get` and `TestMode3_List` only set expectations on the shared `m := &mock.Mock{}` via `m.On("Get"...)` / `m.On("List"...)` and never assert that the legacy mock was not invoked. Because both `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `us := storageMock{m, s}` share the same `mock.Mock`, an accidental call to `LegacyStorage.Get`/`LegacyStorage.List` would still satisfy the same `"Get"`/`"List"` expectation and the test could pass, unlike the old commented-out test which explicitly checked legacy call counts were 0.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:26 — No case where Storage succeeds and Legacy fails or times out, so the async error path, the 10s timeout, and the legacy error metric are never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, Mode3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines with `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, errors.New("legacy ... timeout"))` and records legacy durations via `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). The new tests in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` cover storage success and storage failure cases, but none set up the legacy mock to fail while storage succeeds (nor simulate/force the timeout path), so the async legacy-error branch and its metric recording are not exercised by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:63 — Metrics are never checked, so wrong metric calls go uncaught: legacy duration on storage failure (mode3.go:45,129), storage duration for the legacy DeleteCollection (mode3.go:166), and name passed as kind (mode3.go:106).
matched_golden_ids: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly points out a wrong metric call: "legacy duration on storage failure (mode3.go:45,129)", which aligns with the golden issue that, in DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection, a storage failure incorrectly records legacy duration instead of storage duration. Although it mentions additional metric issues, it includes the same underlying bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go:132 — The mode 3 integration runs reuse doPlaylistTests, which checks the legacy API right after k8s writes; with async legacy writes this is either racy, or it never checks the legacy SQL store because reads go through storage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Mode3 dual-writer behavior to perform legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines with a timeout (e.g., Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go now `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.* ... }()`). The playlist integration tests add new Mode3 runs that reuse `doPlaylistTests` without any visible synchronization/awaiting of the async legacy side effects (pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go adds several `mode 3` subtests but no waits). If `doPlaylistTests` asserts legacy-side effects immediately after writes, this could become racy/flaky; alternatively, if reads are through Storage, the Mode3 integration might not actually validate legacy persistence. However, the diff does not show `doPlaylistTests`, so the exact behavior can’t be verified from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:119 — TestMode3_Get shadows the package-level registry p with a local one while other tests share the global p, so metric state leaks across tests and is not isolated for assertions.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, most tests call `NewDualWriter(Mode3, ls, us, p)` using an unscoped `p` (implying a package-level registry). But `TestMode3_Get` explicitly creates `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` locally, shadowing the package-level `p`. This inconsistency is visible in the diff and can lead to shared registry state (and potential collector double-registration/flakiness) across the other tests, while `TestMode3_Get` is isolated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go:65 — No coverage for nil options: every mode3 method dereferences options.Kind and would panic, but tests always pass non-nil options.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, several Mode3 methods now log with `options.Kind` (and/or `options.ResourceVersion`) without nil checks: Create (`options.Kind`), Get (`options.Kind`), List (`options.Kind`, `options.ResourceVersion`), Delete (`options.Kind`), Update (`options.Kind`), and DeleteCollection (`options.Kind`, plus `listOptions.ResourceVersion`). If any caller passes nil options, these would panic. The new/updated tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go always pass non-nil `&metav1.*Options{}` / `&metainternalversion.ListOptions{}` and thus don’t cover this edge case. Whether nil is permitted by the interface contract isn’t verifiable from the diff, so this is best treated as a missing edge-case/robustness test or guard rather than a confirmed functional bug.
